name: Corinth
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Corinth, TX 2026
seo_description: Free Christmas at the Commons in Corinth, TX on Dec 19: Santa photos, an ice rink and a snow tube slide at the Commons at Agora, plus local history.
lede: The story of Christmas in Corinth begins with a railroad stop named in 1880 and a city incorporated on September 19, 1960. Its big holiday night is Christmas at the Commons, a City of Corinth celebration at the Commons at Agora, across the street from City Hall.
sections: A railroad name and a fast growing town

The Handbook of Texas says Corinth, about six miles southeast of Denton, was named by the Dallas and Wichita Railway in 1880 and celebrated its 100th anniversary in 1980. The City of Corinth says it was incorporated on September 19, 1960. Development along Interstate 35 in the 1970s helped the population grow from 461 in 1970 to 11,325 in 2000 and 22,690 by 2021. The Handbook notes that some residents were independent farmers, while most commuted to nearby cities for work.

The Commons at Agora, at 3280 Agora Way, sits directly across from Corinth City Hall. The city calls it an iconic gathering space and a central hub for community activities, events and festivals, in what it describes as a vibrant downtown district. It has a stage, a playground, a boardwalk and an interactive water feature. The city also runs Friday Night Flicks outdoor movies and the Agora Music Fest concert series there, and its 2025 comprehensive plan calls for a community gathering space named Downtown Corinth.

DCTA's A-train station list has no Corinth stop. Its stations are the Downtown Denton Transit Center, MedPark, Highland Village/Lewisville Lake, Old Town and Hebron, plus Trinity Mills Station in Carrollton, which DART also serves. On Saturday, December 5, 2026, DCTA runs Santa at the Station from the Downtown Denton Transit Center. Corinth itself was named by a railway in 1880, so families who want train history can visit the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco, the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano or the M-Line Trolley in Dallas.

faq: How did Corinth get its name?

The Handbook of Texas says the Dallas and Wichita Railway named Corinth in 1880. The community celebrated its 100th anniversary in 1980. It sits about six miles southeast of Denton in Denton County, and its growth took off after businesses developed along Interstate 35 in the 1970s.
When did Corinth become a city?

The City of Corinth says it was incorporated on September 19, 1960. The Handbook of Texas lists 461 residents in 1970, 11,325 in 2000 and 22,690 in 2021, so most of Corinth's growth has come in the last half century.
Where is Christmas at the Commons in Corinth?

Christmas at the Commons is at the Commons at Agora, 3280 Agora Way, Corinth, TX 76208, directly across from Corinth City Hall. In 2026 it is on Saturday, December 19, from 3 to 8 pm. The City of Corinth runs it, and a sensory-friendly hour is listed from 3 to 4 pm.
What is there for kids at Christmas at the Commons?

The City of Corinth lists photos with Santa, an ice skating rink, a snow tube slide, a make your own holiday cookie station, holiday performances, food trucks and local vendors. A sensory-friendly hour runs from 3 to 4 pm. The event is listed as free.
What else happens at the Commons at Agora?

The city describes it as a hub for community events and festivals. It has a stage, a playground, a boardwalk, an interactive water feature and picnic areas, and it hosts Friday Night Flicks outdoor movies and the Agora Music Fest concerts. It is open for public use from 6 am to 10 pm when no event is scheduled.
Is there a Santa train near Corinth?

Corinth has no A-train stop. DCTA runs Santa at the Station on Saturday, December 5, 2026, from the Downtown Denton Transit Center, with check in at 9:30 am and a 10 am departure to Trinity Mills Station. Tickets are $1.50 for ages 6 and up and are sold online only.
